video.title: The Most Profitable Solo Business You've Never Heard Of

summary: Brett describes DesignJoy, a solo productized design subscription that he says he launched on Product Hunt and grew while keeping his full-time job. He explains its self-serve offer, rapid delivery, pricing increases, workload, and use of AI tools. The conversation also covers possible productized services, including AI-first development, branding, copywriting, video clipping, thumbnails, and podcast editing. A key takeaway is that AI can speed up digital service work, while distribution, client demand, design judgment, and human delivery still matter.

speakers.name: Brett
speakers.description: DesignJoy founder; surname is not stated clearly in the transcript.

ideas.name: DesignJoy productized design subscription
ideas.one_liner: A self-serve subscription for digital design work, delivered by a solo designer.
ideas.business_model: Monthly subscription or retainer; clients can pause and resume.
ideas.customer: Companies and startups that need branding, websites, social media assets, presentation decks, or other digital design.
ideas.problem: Traditional agencies can be expensive and slow, and hiring contractors can mean paying when there is no work.
ideas.offer: Clients subscribe through the website, pay without calls or proposals, and receive design work, often with a homepage returned the next day. Work is handled one request at a time.

pricing.notes: Brett says clients can pause their subscription. He does not give the current exact price after dialing it back.

acquisition_channels.details: Brett submitted DesignJoy to Product Hunt and reached number four on the daily list.

quote.text: Usually, you get instant customers with it. And it's totally free. You just have to have the network of people to upvoted
quote.speaker: Brett

acquisition_channels.details: He asked friends and family from his hometown school network on Facebook to upvote the Product Hunt submission.

quote.text: My personal network was my friends and family I went to school with on Facebook. That was all I had at the time.
quote.speaker: Brett

acquisition_channels.details: He says he shared his story on forums while anonymous and without an audience.

quote.text: No, no audience, I literally shared my story on forums. That's it.
quote.speaker: Brett

ideas.delivery: Brett does the design work himself. Clients submit digital requests through the service; work includes branding, logos, website design and development, social media material, and presentation decks. Requests are handled one at a time. He says AI now helps with requirements, UX thinking, and producing some kinds of assets.
unit_economics_claims: Brett says DesignJoy has generated about USD 1 million a year.
He says monthly expenses are about USD 1,000, excluding taxes.
He says net profit has averaged USD 60,000 to USD 80,000 per month, with a peak of USD 200,000 and a low of USD 40,000.
He says he has handled as many as 50 clients at a time.
ideas.startup_cost: Brett says there were very little costs beyond the time he invested; no amount is stated.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Brett says he had the idea Friday, built it Saturday, launched Sunday, and saw about USD 10,000 on the first day. The exact elapsed time from launch to payment is not stated.

acquisition.how: Product Hunt submission and a self-serve site can be prepared and monitored with software. The launch still depended on a personal network and the service needs ongoing distribution. In the UK, favor inbound channels and consent-based promotion; do not automate unsolicited marketing to individuals or sole traders.

onboarding.how: A website can take payment and accept requests without a sales call, with occasional human review for fit, scope, or unclear briefs.

delivery.how: A designer must make and review each client deliverable. AI can assist with requirements, UX, and assets, but the transcript describes Brett personally doing the design work.

billing.how: Recurring subscriptions and pause or resume billing can be handled by billing software, with a person resolving exceptions.

support.how: Routine request intake can be structured, but client feedback, judgment, and design decisions still need human attention.

uk_applicability.notes: A digital design subscription can serve UK businesses in the same basic way. Pricing, tax handling, and contract terms would need to suit the local market.

risks: Brett says rapid revenue growth and a large client load led him to work himself nearly to death and into hospital.
He says increasing prices did not reduce demand as he expected; it sometimes increased demand by moving the offer into another category.
He says monthly recurring revenue swings with churn and clients pausing.
The business remains dependent on Brett's personal design capacity, so it is not close to unattended delivery.

tactics.name: Launch through Product Hunt with a small existing network
steps: Build a simple service site and make the offer clear enough to buy without a call.
Submit the product to Product Hunt on launch day.
Ask friends and family to support the launch; Brett used his school network on Facebook to request upvotes.
Share the founder story on forums, even without an established audience.
Treat marketplace exposure as a launch spike, then build a repeatable acquisition channel.

tactics.name: Make a service purchasable without a sales process
steps: Turn a broad custom service into a clearly described package.
Let customers select and pay on the website instead of requesting a quote and attending several meetings.

warnings.warning: Brett says the business grew to a workload that nearly killed him and led to a hospital stay. He later improved his systems, became more selective with clients, and reduced his hours.
Raising prices did not reliably curb demand; Brett says price increases sometimes increased demand by moving the service into a different category.
Monthly recurring revenue is volatile because clients churn or pause subscriptions.
The Tea dating app suffered a data leak, according to the guest.
The guest says AI output can fall short when the user lacks design taste, and the tools are not yet equivalent to an experienced designer.
AI-first development can lead non-technical users into repeated troubleshooting loops and high token bills; security, payments, hosting, and support still require capable people.

The host promotes his own community and podcast and offers a referral payment for people whose story is selected for an interview. This is a promotional conflict for the host, not evidence about the guest's business results.

lessons.lesson: Make it possible to buy a clearly defined service without a quote request, sales call, or several meetings.

lessons.lesson: Customers may value speed and a short time to value, even when a slower process offers more customization.

quote.text: You know, a lot of companies value speed over quality as weird as that is to say.
quote.speaker: Brett

lessons.lesson: A small personal network can help seed a marketplace launch, but the launch itself does not remove the need for ongoing distribution.

lessons.lesson: When a digital product is easy to build and copy, distribution and brand distinction become more important.
